name: Elihu
overview: Elihu was a male descendant of the tribe of Manasseh who played a notable role as a captain of thousands. He is recognized for defecting to David during the time David was at Ziklag. This allegiance marks Elihu as a significant military leader among those who joined David's cause.
namesAndTitles: The name Elihu means 'y-h-v-h is [my] G-d,' reflecting a declaration of faith in the LORD. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:20, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theistic affirmation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Elihu as a descendant of Manasseh, linking him to this particular tribe of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elihu's significance lies in his military leadership and his decision to join David at Ziklag, which contributed to David's growing support among Israelite tribes. As a captain of thousands, his defection to David represents a pivotal moment in the consolidation of David's power. His presence among David's followers highlights the divine providence in uniting leaders from various tribes under David's kingship.
